record.nameMeaning: "Different lizard", for its unusually lightweight vertebrae
record.oneLiner: The apex predatory theropod of the Late Jurassic Morrison Formation.
record.description: Allosaurus was a large bipedal predator with a light but robust skull bearing dozens of sharp, serrated teeth, small three-fingered hands, and a long muscular tail. It averaged about 8.5 m long, with the largest specimens near 9.7 m. As the most abundant large predator of the Morrison Formation, it was the apex predator, likely hunting ornithopods, stegosaurids and sauropods.

notableFacts.text: Its light skull bore dozens of sharp, serrated teeth.
The most abundant large predator of the Morrison Formation.
Whether it hunted in packs or was solitary remains debated.
